extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of psychology/psychoanalysis and humor theory; readers studying mechanisms of wit
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative criteria and production principles for witticisms (jokes, jests) as presented in a psychoanalytic/theoretical account of wit. Focuses on techniques, tendencies, pleasure-mechanisms, and situational factors that make wit effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasure from gratification of a tendency (tendency-wit)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The pleasure in tendency-wit results from the fact that a tendency, whose gratification would otherwise remain unfulfilled, is actually gratified.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tendency-wit produces pleasure because a wished-for aggressive/critical/obscene impulse (a tendency) that would normally be blocked is satisfied by the jest. Examples: replies that answer an insult with another, or an affront substituted for expert opinion. This is a central evaluative dimension: does the joke enact the gratification of a suppressed tendency?

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiation of external vs internal hindrance
rubrics_metrics.description: Two cases: gratification opposed by an external hindrance (power/position of target) or by an internal hindrance (inner resistance, aesthetic sense, reason).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text differentiates situations where wit eludes external constraints (e.g., insulting a socially powerful person by a clever retort) from those where wit removes an inner inhibition. The removal of inner hindrance (inhibition) often yields greater pleasure because it relieves psychic expenditure; use examples (Serenissimus, Wendell Phillips) when evaluating intensity of effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy in the expenditure of inhibitions or suppressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Freud's formulation: “economy in the expenditure of inhibitions or suppressions” is proposed as the secret of the pleasurable effect of tendency-wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleasure from wit corresponds to saving psychic energy—either by removing an existing inhibition (relief) or avoiding formation of a new one (economy). Evaluate jokes by how much psychic expenditure they obviate or save.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two intrinsic pleasure-sources: wit-technique and wit-tendency
rubrics_metrics.description: “The latter itself has two intrinsic sources, namely, the wit-technique and the wit-tendency.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should consider both the formal technique (wordplay, sound, structure) and the tendency/content (aggression, cynicism, self-criticism). A strong witticism often combines an effective technique with a salient tendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-pleasure: focus on sound over sense (word-play)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasure arises when the psychic focus is directed upon the sound instead of upon the sense of the word (word-disguise takes place of meaning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate use of puns, homophones, rhyme, alliteration, or phonetic ambiguity that privilege acoustic association over semantic relation. The greater the ‘short-circuit’ from one idea to a remote other via sound, the stronger the economy and potential pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unification and similar-sounding techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Second group of technical means: unification, similar sounding words, manifold application, modification of familiar idioms, allusions to quotations — “one always discovers something familiar where one expects to find something new instead.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These techniques create pleasure by discovering the familiar (recognition) in an unexpected place. Evaluate a witticism for the cleverness and economy of its unifying device and whether it yields recognition/rediscovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor of actuality (temporal/current-interest relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of actual persons, things, or events often provides a prolific and transitory source of pleasure; witticisms tied to current affairs borrow vitality and can fade when the underlying interest lapses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess topicality: jokes that rely on contemporary events can be highly effective in-context but lose force over time. Distinguish perennial techniques from actuality-dependent humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasure of recognition / rediscovery of the familiar
rubrics_metrics.description: “To discover the familiar is pleasurable... the recognition ‘per se’ ... through the alleviation of the psychic expenditure, is pleasurable.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure how much a joke produces a pleasurable recognition (e.g., linking two disparate ideas under a familiar term). Recognition is a central pleasure-source distinct from a sense of power or surmounting difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Techniques of thought-wit: false logic, displacement, absurdity, representation through the opposite
rubrics_metrics.description: Thought-wit includes false logic, displacement, absurdity, representation through the opposite, and related devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate these devices for how they ease psychic expenditure (they make it easier to deviate from strict reasoning), and for their ability to make the nonsensical acceptable by clever framing. Examples in text: absurdities that appear only apparent, representation through the opposite, displacement-witticisms (shnorrer examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of object-association by word-association (sound-based short-circuits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit may replace object-association by word-association, allowing acoustic/phonetic links to take precedence over referential meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the economy achieved when word-association permits a rapid mental leap from one idea-domain to another (e.g., linking kitchen to politics via a single word). This short-circuit reduces psychic work and is pleasurable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasure in nonsense regained via disinhibition (children, intoxication, pathology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Children and adults under toxic influence (alcohol) show a pleasure in nonsense; such states weaken inhibitions permitting nonsensical connections that are normally suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or producing wit, note whether the effect depends on lowered critical faculties (audience intoxication, childlike play). Such sources of pleasure are qualitatively different and often rely on a temporary state rather than purely intellectual cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play vs Jest distinction: juvenile play vs adult jest that appeases reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Play is the child's free experimentation with words/thoughts; the jest aims to bring about the pleasure of play while appeasing the protesting reason—making the senseless make sense sufficiently to pass scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective adult wit (jest) must carve out a space where childish playfulness is tolerated by reason: it selects word-material or thought-situations that will stand the test of criticism. Evaluate whether a witticism successfully balances playful freedom with acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense-in-nonsense requirement (avoidance of pure nonsense)
rubrics_metrics.description: A witticism, though it may appear nonsensical from one point of view, must ‘appear full of meaning or at least acceptable from another.’ If not, it is relegated to ‘nonsense.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the joke supplies an alternate interpretation or framing that renders its absurdity acceptable; outright meaningless utterances lack wit unless reframed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-criticism / insider perspective enhances tendency-wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-criticism (criticism directed against one’s own person or composite personality like ‘one’s own people’) produces a favorable case for tendency-wit because the speaker’s interest enables subjective determination of the wit-work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insider jokes (e.g., community self-mockery) can be more effective because they bypass hostile projection and show awareness of shortcomings; evaluate the authenticity and self-directedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit-work’s safeguarding against reason (the unique technique of wit)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The technique... which is peculiar to and belongs to wit alone consists in a process of safeguarding the use of this pleasure-forming means against the protest of reason.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a production criterion: wit must devise strategies (framing, ambiguity, ironic stance) that let pleasure-forming, play-like devices survive critical scrutiny. Judge how well a witticism protects its play-pleasures from rational rejection.
